title: CUB sparse-keypoint phenomenon reliability audit across three 10-shot episodes
purpose: Final train-only reliability audit. This is not a new method experiment and cannot rescue the failed active-selection or gradient-safety gates.

data.independence_note: Episodes are independently sampled without replacement within each class. They are not forced disjoint because six official-train classes contain only 29 images.

arms.GLOBAL: Global average pooling; classification loss on all fold-training images.
arms.RANDOM_K1: PrPool architecture; exactly one uniformly selected keypoint-annotated fold-training image per class.
arms.FULL_KEYPOINT_ORACLE: PrPool architecture; keypoint supervision on every fold-training image.

annotation_sampling.candidate_information: image ID, class label, and fold only; keypoint coordinates are forbidden during selection
annotation_sampling.budget: exactly one selected image per class in every fold-training set

primary_endpoints: paired Random-K1 minus Global OOF balanced-accuracy gain in each episode
paired Full-Oracle minus Global OOF balanced-accuracy gain in each episode
Random-K1 class negative-transfer rate versus paired Global in each episode
episode-pooled class recall delta and worst-class damage

go_no_go.sparse_value_reliable_if: Random-K1 mean gain is at least 3.0 pp and at least two of three episode gains are at least 3.0 pp.
go_no_go.positive_ceiling_reliable_if: Full-Oracle mean gain is at least 2.0 pp and at least two of three episode gains are at least 2.0 pp.
go_no_go.class_risk_reliable_if: Random-K1 negative-transfer class-rate range across episodes is at most 10 percentage points.
go_no_go.overall_go: All three reliability conditions pass and official test access remains zero.
go_no_go.on_go: The empirical phenomenon is reliable enough to formulate a new class-level annotation-allocation or worst-class-risk question; do not claim the failed selectors or gradient-safety mechanism.
go_no_go.on_no_go: Stop the CUB sparse-keypoint direction and change dataset/topic.
